cards.title: WEAVE: objective-led education and feedback
cards.practice: Wonder defines audience needs; Explore sets learning goals; Action implements; Verify examines learning; Echo uses feedback for the next revision.
cards.reflection: The team framework connects activity choices to audience needs and subsequent improvement.
cards.adaptation: Use the phases to explain why each activity is included and how understanding will be checked.

cards.title: Plant-to-product route-card workshop
cards.location: Joint design proposal: green manufacturing route puzzle
cards.practice: The proposal asks learners to arrange raw-material, conversion and product cards, compare two project routes and justify a new waste-use choice.
cards.reflection: The proposal recommends an accessible process-level story and lists learner explanations and decision reasons as intended evaluation records.
cards.adaptation: Use a printed route puzzle with short group explanations in a classroom without laboratory equipment. Treat the new agenda as a proposed adaptation.

cards.title: Adapt the detection activity to available equipment
cards.practice: The team draft describes replacing a fluorescence-identification activity after a pre-test did not yield a clear distinction; digital pH meters offered an alternative.
cards.reflection: The narrative links the redesign to an observed implementation limitation and the partner laboratory resources.
cards.adaptation: Pre-test the educational task. For a classroom-only plan, use prepared evidence cards instead of assuming access to an instrument.

cards.title: DNA builder: pair and inspect bases
cards.practice: The implemented resource lets users assemble nucleotides and inspect base pairing and a two- or three-dimensional helix.
cards.reflection: The repository describes functionality; it does not report an evaluated learning gain.
cards.adaptation: Use a projected worked example followed by paper base-pair cards and a short explanation task.

cards.title: Fermentation map: connect microbes and familiar foods
cards.practice: The resource connects familiar fermented foods with microbial conditions through a regional map and virtual lab.
cards.reflection: The catalog records the resource purpose and interface, rather than an educational-impact measurement.
cards.adaptation: Ask learners to compare two familiar examples and state which conditions a microbial process needs.

cards.title: Heidelberg: explanation, practice and quiz
cards.practice: Heidelberg combined illustrated protocols, calculators and quizzes; learner feedback informed the addition of laboratory videos.
cards.reflection: The report links complementary formats to feedback from students and educators.
cards.adaptation: Follow one short illustrated explanation with a worked example and a check-for-understanding question.
cards.evidenceQuote: Our platform features lab protocols, interactive calculators, module quizzes and videos

cards.title: BUCT: drawing-to-clay learning with individual support
cards.location: Equ-Globalizing: children with special educational needs
cards.practice: BUCT used illustrated explanations, drawings and colored-clay models, with individual facilitator support.
cards.reflection: Teacher reflections and participant creations were used as feedback about participation and understanding.
cards.adaptation: Offer drawing and tactile options; collect a learner explanation and a facilitator observation rather than relying on speed or a written quiz.
cards.evidenceQuote: the children transformed their two-dimensional sketches into three-dimensional models using colored clay.

cards.title: Peking: cross-disciplinary digital BioQuest
cards.practice: The team ran a digital challenge using synthetic-biology scenarios and multiple-choice questions for students across university departments.
cards.reflection: The stated aim was interdisciplinary dialogue rather than a knowledge examination.
cards.adaptation: Pair each scenario with a short justification and discussion; choose examples appropriate to the new audience.
cards.evidenceQuote: designed not to test knowledge, but to spark interdisciplinary dialogues.

cards.location: 2.2 Education for Junior High School Students — Feedback and Reflection
cards.title: DEPU: explanation followed by fruit DNA extraction
cards.practice: The junior-high workshop combined a synthetic-biology presentation with fruit DNA extraction.
cards.reflection: Some participants found the presentation too basic; the team proposed adjusting future depth to prior knowledge.
cards.adaptation: Check prior knowledge first, connect each observation to a concept, and collect explanations after the demonstration.
cards.evidenceQuote: some students found the presentation content relatively basic.

cards.title: Barcelona-UB: modular fruit DNA extraction resource
cards.practice: The toolkit provides a fruit-DNA activity with comprehension questions for high schools.
cards.reflection: The page describes the experimental resource; the cited school had implemented other modules and planned this one.
cards.adaptation: Use the experiment as a resource to adapt, with a concept check and locally confirmed materials.
cards.evidenceQuote: Comprehension questions at the end help ensure students understand the biology behind the experiment.

cards.location: Yeast Adventure: Cell Explorer Card Game — Target Audience and Project Description
cards.title: NACIS-Shanghai: cell-structure tabletop game
cards.practice: The team describes a cell-themed tabletop game for children, with card collection and age-adapted modes.
cards.reflection: The page includes a campus demonstration and participant comments; these do not establish effects for a new adaptation.
cards.adaptation: Simplify the cards for the chosen age group and ask players to explain one structure-function connection.
cards.evidenceQuote: A strategic tabletop game that introduces organelles and enzymes through family-friendly play.

cards.title: NNU-CHINA: The Secret of the Rainbow Orchard
cards.practice: The team created a picture book about pesticide choices and greener agriculture for children.
cards.reflection: This section describes the resource and intended learning purpose, without a separate measured learning-gain result.
cards.adaptation: Pause at a decision in the story and ask learners to explain a choice using a scientific reason.
cards.evidenceQuote: The Secret of the Rainbow Orchard

cards.title: Institut-Le-Rosey-CH: discussing de-extinction
cards.practice: The team organized a community debate on de-extinction, with opposing teams and a chair.
cards.reflection: The stated motivation was responding to misinformation through discussion of science and ethical concerns.
cards.adaptation: Provide a short evidence pack, separate factual claims from value judgments, and collect reasons before and after discussion.
cards.evidenceQuote: our team organized an informational debate to educate our community on the science behind de-extinction.
